newsitem.title: USA: P.A.M sees momentum continuing through 97.
newsitem.headline: P.A.M sees momentum continuing through 97.

text.p: P.A.M. Transportation Services, Inc said Thursday it expected the momentum of a strong economy and lower fuel prices to continue through 1997.

"We see a stronger economy this year, business is robust, and fuel prices are at last exhibiting a downward trend," said president Robert Weaver. "These positive developments, together with our management team's continued focus on boosting revenues and containing costs, are reflected in much improved results of operations. We are optimistic that this momentum will continue throughout 1997."

The company Thursday reported net income of $1,284,245 or $.16 per share for the quarter ended March 31, 1997. These results compare to net income of $759,289 or $.10 per share for the same period of 1996. Revenues of $32,629,999 were reported for the first quarter of 1997 compared to first quarter 1996 revenues of $23,532,155.
